question: Is Trent Alexander-Arnold more valuable to Liverpool's attacking play than Andy Robertson in 2023-24?

on_off_splits.delta_summary: PPG +0.21 with TAA on a meaningful 26-vs-12 sample. Bradley + Gomez handled the role serviceably.

scout_notes.author: The Athletic — James Pearce
scout_notes.summary: TAA's inverted midfield role was Klopp's primary build-up mechanism through autumn; his absences disrupted Liverpool's ability to attack vs low blocks. Key-pass volume remained league-leading despite 26 starts.

on_off_splits.delta_summary: Essentially zero PPG delta on a 19-vs-19 sample. Tsimikas covered effectively, masking attacking output drop.

scout_notes.author: The Athletic — James Pearce
scout_notes.summary: Robertson's season was disrupted by a shoulder injury in October; on return he was visibly below his 2021-22 peak — overlapping runs reduced, crossing volume down 30%. Cover (Tsimikas) was competent.

dossier.context_notes: Liverpool finished 3rd in 2023-24, Klopp's final season. Both full-backs missed extended time — TAA hamstring (Jan-Feb), Robertson shoulder (Oct-Jan). Direct comparison is fair: both played enough to compare team-share contribution. The question framing ('attacking play') biases toward progressive-pass and key-pass shares, where TAA leads.

__note__: Investigator case — full-back comparison. Tests that defensive-position players generate sufficient attacking-play data to be evaluated under the framework. Balance scorer should PASS — both subjects have matching field coverage.
